rfm_tuples.R: As a percentage of gross loans, excluding loans held for sale, plus OREO, our non-performing assets increased to 1.01% at December 31, 2024, from 0.48% at December 31, 2023. The non-performing portfolio loan, excluding loans held for sale, coverage ratio, defined as the allowance for credit losses to non-performing loans, excluding loans held for sale, decreased to 98.98% at December 31, 2024, from 221.58% at December 31, 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: self_text — verify the magnitude of NPL deterioration and coverage erosion against the same filing's financial tables and FDIC Call Report nonaccrual time series.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FDIC Call Report NCLNLS (nonaccrual + 90+ days) for Cathay Bank: 2024-03-31 $105.6M; 2024-06-30 $110.6M; 2024-09-30 $169.6M (+53% QoQ); 2024-12-31 $173.1M. 10-K MD&A reports total non-accrual jumped $102.5M (+154%) to $169.2M, total NPL $173.2M (+135% YoY), and allowance coverage of NPL collapsed from 222% to 99%. The credit deterioration is DISCLOSED, but represents a real and severe credit-cycle inflection for a 'boring' regional bank.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: NPL more than doubled in 12 months and allowance coverage fell to just under 1.0x — that is a hard-to-paper-over credit deterioration. Honesty framework: disclosure is faithful (so framework can't catch them lying), but the underlying credit signal is severe for a regional bank with 52% CRE concentration.

rfm_tuples.R: Total CRE loans represented 289% of total risk-based capital as of December 31, 2024, and 292% as of December 31, 2023, which were within the Bank's internal limit of 400% of total capital. ... Commercial real estate loans increased $304.2 million, or 3.1%, to $10.03 billion at December 31, 2024 ... Total commercial real estate loans accounted for 51.8% of gross loans at December 31, 2024, compared to 49.8% at December 31, 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: self_text — derived check that CRE concentration sits one notch below the 300% regulatory guidance trigger, and CRE grew $304M YoY while NPLs surged. Verify against MD&A tables (CRE balance and capital ratio).
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K MD&A directly confirms: CRE = $10.03B / 51.8% of gross loans / 289% of risk-based capital, vs 2006 federal interagency CRE supervisory criterion of 300%. The bank is one rate-environment shock from crossing the regulatory threshold that triggers heightened supervisory scrutiny.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: CRE 289% of capital is technically 'under the 400% internal limit' as claimed — but it is just barely under the FFIEC's 300% guidance threshold that triggers regulatory CRE concentration review. Framing this as 'within limits' obscures the proximity to the actual binding regulatory threshold.

rfm_tuples.R: Net interest margin, defined as net interest income to average interest-earning assets, was 3.04% in 2024 compared to 3.45% in 2023. ... For the year ended December 31, 2024, we reported net income of $286.0 million, or $3.95 per diluted share, compared to net income of $354.1 million, or $4.86 per diluted share, in 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: self_text — verify earnings compression magnitude and link to NIM compression of 41 bps YoY.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Confirmed: NIM compressed from 3.45% to 3.04% (-41bps); interest expense rose +32.1% YoY to $660.9M while interest income only rose +7.5%; net income fell $68.1M (-19.2%); ROA 1.22% vs 1.56%; ROE 10.18% vs 13.56%. Provision for credit losses rose to $37.5M (vs $26.0M in 2023, vs $14.5M in 2022) — a 2.6x increase in two years.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest disclosure of an industry-typical NIM squeeze, but combined with surging credit costs the earnings power is materially impaired. Banks with double-digit ROE base-case running through a NIM-squeeze + credit-cycle inflection deserve a real haircut.

rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2024, and 2023, the Company had $9.43 billion and $8.71 billion, respectively, of uninsured deposits outstanding.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: derived — given the SVB/Signature 2023 episode, uninsured-deposit ratio matters; verify against total deposits and prior-year comparable.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total deposits at Dec-31-2024 = $19.69B per Business overview. Uninsured deposits $9.43B = 47.9% of total. Up $720M YoY (+8.3%) — uninsured deposit base grew faster than insured. 86.7% of jumbo CDs ($250K+) on deposit ≥2 years. This is a Chinese-American community bank with sticky relationship deposits, but the 48% uninsured share is elevated relative to peer regionals.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Half the deposit base is uninsured at a bank with deteriorating credit metrics. While the niche customer base (long-tenured relationships) provides some stability, 48% uninsured is structurally fragile in a stress scenario.

rfm_tuples.R: Net charge-offs for 2024 were $29.7 million, or 0.15% of average loans, compared to net charge-offs of $17.6 million for 2023, or 0.09% of average loans, and net charge-offs of $2.6 million for 2022, or 0.01% of average loans.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: self_text — verify three-year trajectory of charge-off normalization.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Confirmed: Net charge-offs progression 2022 $2.6M (0.01%) → 2023 $17.6M (0.09%) → 2024 $29.7M (0.15%). That is a 11x increase in two years and a 69% increase YoY. Still low in absolute terms (15bps) but the second-derivative is accelerating with NPL inflow.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is accurate. The 15bps NCO is still well below stress-cycle levels (banks typically peak at 100-300bps in a real downturn), but the trajectory shows credit normalization is underway and not yet stabilized.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K filed 2025-02-28] Total non-performing portfolio assets increased $103.0 million, or 110.4%, to $196.3 million at December 31, 2024. rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: claim_evolution — compare credit-quality narrative between 2024 10-K (filed 2025-02-28) and the immediately following Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09, six days before cutoff). Does Q1 confirm a one-quarter peak or further deterioration?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q shows modest sequential improvement (NPA $173.7M vs $196.3M YE2024, -11.5% QoQ; coverage ratio improved to 119% from 99%). HOWEVER non-accrual loans of $154.6M at Mar-31-2025 are STILL +57.6% above $98.1M at Mar-31-2024 — the YoY trajectory remains deeply negative. No new disclosed credit cliff in Q1, but the implied stabilization is fragile (only one quarter of improvement on a still-elevated base).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Pre-cutoff claim evolution shows the 10-K's NPL spike was not yet a one-off — non-accruals remain elevated and YoY growth is still +58%. Management is not hiding it, but the 'getting better' Q1 framing is supported by only one quarter of data on top of a 12-month tripling.

rfm_tuples.R: Auditor Name: KPMG LLP, Auditor Location: Los Angeles, California, Auditor Firm ID: 185. Item 9. Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure — Not Applicable.

rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: insider_vs_calendar — given that NPLs surged Q3 2024 (Sep-30 FDIC NPL $169.6M vs Jun-30 $110.6M, +53% QoQ), look for clustered insider open-market sales around the 10-Q filings that disclosed each leg of the credit deterioration.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 15 open-market sales totaling $6.12M during the 16-month pre-cutoff window. Cluster #1: 2024-07-29 (after Q2 NPL leg) — Wu sold $904K, Tang $343K, Bingham $269K, total ~$1.5M. Cluster #2: 2024-11-01 to 2024-11-08 (immediately around Q3 10-Q with the big NPL jump) — Wu sold $3.05M (60K shares) including 40K @$52.87 on the SAME DAY (Nov 8) the Q3 10-Q was filed; Tang sold $157K; Lo sold $42K — total Nov cluster ~$3.25M, of which Peter Wu (Executive Chairman / founder family) accounted for $3.05M (94% of the cluster).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Peter Wu's 40,000-share / $2.1M sale on Nov 8, 2024 — the exact day the Q3 10-Q disclosed the +53% QoQ nonaccrual surge — is a textbook insider-vs-calendar signal. The 'safe harbor' explanation is a 10b5-1 plan, but the magnitude and date alignment with the Q3 credit news is a meaningful Mode-B finding the disclosure itself does not surface. Cumulative pre-cutoff insider sales of $6.1M while NPLs tripled is not a confidence vote.

rfm_tuples.R: At December 31, 2024, the Company's Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio of 13.54%, total risk-based capital ratio of 15.08%, and Tier 1 leverage capital ratio of 10.96% ... continue to place the Company in the 'well capitalized' category.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Capital ratios confirmed; bank paid $216M to holdco in 2024 (vs $134M in 2023, $232.8M in 2022). Bancorp continues $1.36 annual dividend (paid 2022, 2023, 2024 unchanged). Retained earnings available for cash dividend restricted to $433.6M. Treasury share count rose to 20.75M from 18.72M (≈2.0M-share repurchase during 2024, ~3% of float) — capital being returned even as provision/charge-offs climbed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital ratios are healthy, but the bank chose to repurchase ~2M shares and maintain the full dividend through 2024 while NPLs more than doubled and coverage ratio fell to <1.0x. That is procyclical capital deployment — consistent with management not perceiving 2024 as a credit cycle inflection.

rfm_tuples.R: We recorded a provision for credit losses of $37.5 million in the year ended December 31, 2024. ... The allowance allocated to commercial real estate loans was $79.6 million at December 31, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: derived — given $169.2M non-accrual loans and only $171.4M total allowance for credit losses (98.98% coverage), is the implied reserve ratio adequate for a CRE-concentrated bank entering credit normalization?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total ACL $171.4M at YE-2024 = 0.88% of $19.36B gross loans. CRE-specific reserve = $79.6M against $10.03B CRE = 0.79% of CRE balance. Peer regional banks with comparable CRE concentration typically reserve 1.0-1.5% of CRE. Coverage of non-accrual loans dropped from 222% to 99% YoY. If non-accrual loans continue rising and recoveries don't materialize, the bank will likely need to take additional provisions in 2025-2026 (forecast not used in scoring; only the structural under-reserving observation).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Reserve build is lagging the NPL inflow. The bank disclosed it ($37.5M provision = only 1.26x of $29.7M NCOs, so reserve barely grew). Coverage <1.0x at the front of a credit normalization cycle is a structurally under-reserved position for a 52% CRE-concentrated regional bank.

summary: Cathay General Bancorp is a Chinese-American community-focused regional bank that experienced a sharp credit cycle inflection during 2024: total NPLs +135% YoY to $173M, nonaccrual loans +154% to $169M, NIM compression of 41bps, net income -19%, and allowance-to-NPL coverage collapsing from 222% to 99%. Disclosure is forthright (KPMG clean opinion, no auditor disagreements, no material weakness), so the framework's lying-detector does NOT identify obscuring. However, two Mode-B findings sharpen the read: (1) CRE concentration at 289% of risk-based capital sits one rate-shock from the 300% regulatory guidance trigger, and the bank is structurally under-reserved at 0.88% ACL/loans heading into a credit normalization; (2) insider open-market sales totaled $6.1M pre-cutoff, with a $3.25M cluster Nov 1-8, 2024 — including Peter Wu's 40,000-share / $2.1M sale on the exact day the Q3 10-Q disclosed the +53% QoQ nonaccrual surge. The Q1 2025 10-Q showed modest sequential improvement (NPA -11.5% QoQ) but non-accruals are still +58% YoY. Verdict: cohort-relative SHORT-tier read on the combination of credit deterioration trajectory + insider-vs-calendar Mode-B finding, despite the honest disclosure profile.
